These devices measure the amount of electricity used in individual units of a building, allowing you to accurately bill tenants for their usage. This can lead to significant cost savings for both you and your tenants.

Understanding Electricity Sub Metering

If you're looking to improve your building's energy efficiency, reduce costs, and gain more control over your utility management, sub metering is the way to go. Sub metering is the process of installing individual meters to measure the consumption of electricity, gas, or water for each tenant in a building or complex. By measuring and tracking energy consumption, you can identify areas of improvement and make more informed decisions about your energy usage.
Benefits of Sub Metering

Sub metering offers several benefits for both property owners and tenants. For property owners, sub metering allows for more accurate billing and promotes fairness and transparency. With sub metering, each tenant is responsible for their individual usage, and billing is based on actual consumption. This helps to eliminate disputes over utility bills and ensures that tenants are paying their fair share.

For tenants, sub metering provides a greater sense of control over their energy usage and costs. By being able to see exactly how much energy they are consuming, tenants can make more informed decisions about their energy usage and adjust their behavior accordingly. This can lead to significant cost savings over time.
Types of Sub Meters
There are several types of sub meters available, each with its own unique features and benefits. The most common types of sub meters include electric sub meters, water sub meters, and gas sub meters.

Electric sub meters are used to measure the consumption of electricity in a building or complex. They can be used to monitor the energy usage of individual tenants or specific areas of a building, such as common areas or shared spaces.

Water sub meters are used to measure the consumption of water in a building or complex. They can be used to monitor the water usage of individual tenants or specific areas of a building, such as irrigation systems or swimming pools.

Gas sub meters are used to measure the consumption of gas in a building or complex. They can be used to monitor the gas usage of individual tenants or specific areas of a building, such as heating systems or gas-powered appliances.
Sub Metering vs. Master Metering

Sub metering differs from master metering in that it provides a more detailed breakdown of energy consumption. Master metering involves installing a single meter to measure the total energy consumption of an entire building or complex. While master metering is a simpler and less expensive option, it doesn't provide the same level of detail as sub metering.

Understanding Local Laws and Regulations

Before implementing a sub-metering system, it's important to research and understand the local laws and regulations governing sub-metering in your area. For example, in New York City, Local Law 88 requires certain buildings to sub-meter their electricity usage and report it to the city. Failure to comply with these regulations can result in hefty fines and penalties.

Compliance with ASHRAE Standards

In addition to local laws and regulations, it's important to ensure that your sub-metering system is compliant with industry standards. The American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) has developed a set of standards for sub-metering that cover everything from meter accuracy to data collection and reporting.

Installation and Maintenance of Sub Meters

Submetering is a process of installing individual meters to measure the consumption of electricity, gas, or water for each tenant in a building or complex. The installation process of submeters is a crucial step to ensure accurate readings and effective utility management. In this section, we will discuss the submeter installation process, maintenance, and accuracy, and compare manual vs. wireless reading.
Submeter Installation Process

The submeter installation process involves several steps, including selecting the appropriate submeter model, installing the submeter, connecting it to the electrical panel, and testing the installation. The installation process requires a licensed electrician to ensure compliance with local regulations and safety standards.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we have a team of experienced professionals who can handle all aspects of submeter installation. Our team will work with you to select the right submeter model and ensure that the installation process is seamless and efficient.
Maintenance and Accuracy

Submeter maintenance is critical to ensure accurate readings and effective utility management. Regular maintenance includes cleaning the submeter, checking for loose connections, and replacing batteries if necessary. Additionally, submeters should be calibrated periodically to ensure accurate readings.

At Axis Meter Solutions, we offer comprehensive maintenance plans to ensure that your submeters are functioning correctly. Our team will perform regular maintenance and calibration to ensure accurate readings and effective utility management.
Manual vs. Wireless Reading

Manual reading involves physically reading the submeter and recording the readings manually. This method is time-consuming and prone to errors. Wireless reading, on the other hand, involves remotely accessing the submeter data, which saves time and reduces the risk of errors.

By accurately billing tenants, you can also reduce disputes and liability issues related to utility expenses.

Sub-metering can help you optimize your utility expenses and increase your return on investment (ROI). With accurate data on energy usage, you can identify areas for improvement and implement energy-saving measures. This can lead to cost savings for both property owners and tenants.
